body:
Tested locally, it works as expected.

I made a project to benchmark loading times and VRAM utilization (with a script to automatically generate textures and materials). I'll upload it later after cleanup.

Some feedback:

- The EditorSpinSlider used for texture LOD configuration is too sensitive when you drag the background of the slider (not the grabber itself). I'm barely moving the mouse here, even when holding <kbd>Shift</kbd> near the end:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4d7c5982-e43b-487b-b3e5-222e44ed19e2

It would be good to fix this issue in EditorSpinSlider somehow (it's not exclusive to this dialog, but it's most noticeable here due to how wide the slider is). Alternatively, it may be better to replace this with a SpinBox instead.

Ok, I'm going to approve the work here from my perspective with the following footnotes: - I'm basing this mostly on testing the work and it doing what it says on the tin, and seeing a lot of value in supporting this logic - From what I can see of the written code, it's well put together and I don't see anything that makes me go "huh, why did he do that". However, my understanding of texture streaming is only high level, I'm not familiar with the best practices and whether there is a better way to solve this. That said, from what I understand of it, this looks good. Going on feedback given by others who are better informed however, I would be confident if we merge this. I have some wishes for improvements, but I feel these all are better served as follow up PRs as they do not effect the core implementation. My two main ones are: - The ability to either set a radius around the player, or maybe use area nodes or something similar, to trigger texture being fully loaded, and to prevent textures from being unloaded when the object using them are within those spaces. This would prevent popping in textures for high detail objects when a player turns around. - Adding key metrics that are live inside of the editor to see the effects of changing the settings in the editor. My suggestion would be to add streaming texture memory, and possibly something like how many actions are actually being taken per second. I'd add them in this dialog:
Style and docs look good, haven't tested
Implementation is looking pretty solid. The previous RDG performance problem I found can be fixed later, but I found an issue with early fragment tests that should be fixed before merge.

Looks great! All my implementation concerns have been addressed and it now works like I wanted it to: self contained and not affecting any of the main rendering systems negatively.

We should merge this now to get user feedback during the dev/beta period. Any further performance improvements can be done after the merge (I already have some I need to do like the RDG issue), this is already a very good baseline.

I'll let @clayjohn do the final approval.

Amazing work! This is looking really good. Let's get this merged ASAP to get as much testing as possible before stable. 

One thing we need to follow up with before release is adding the `sampler2DStreamed` from [Juan's original proposal](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/3177#issuecomment-2278832116). I know this technique doesn't do the funky stuff with indexing into texture arrays. But right now the code is hurting performance for every spatial shader, even if no streaming textures are used since streaming is enabled for every shader if the streaming module is enabled. 

If we use `sampler2DStreamed` then we can define `TEXTURE_STREAMING` only for shaders that actually use a `StreamedTexture2D` and avoid paying the cost for streaming in all shaders. 

At any rate, that's fine to do as a follow up so we can get this PR out the door. Again, great work! I am super happy to see this finally cross the finish line
